result.summary: The image shows a mixed-use urban street with tram tracks embedded in the roadway and buildings situated directly at the sidewalk edge. While sidewalks and basic curb ramps are present, the environment lacks high-visibility crossings and features significant visual obstructions from on-street parking.

hazards.name: Tram tracks
hazards.description: Metal rails embedded in the roadway present a tripping hazard for pedestrians and a slip hazard when wet.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway extending into the distance

hazards.name: Parked cars
hazards.description: Parallel parking along the curb creates visual obstructions, making it difficult for drivers and pedestrians to see each other at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the street

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk
hazards.description: The existing crosswalk markings are worn and difficult to see, reducing driver awareness of the crossing point.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left at the intersection

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace faded markings with continental-style stripes to improve visibility for approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond parked cars.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-scale lighting
interventions.description: Enhance existing street lighting with lower-level fixtures focused on the sidewalk and crossing areas.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, paved sidewalk directly adjacent to a roadway with embedded streetcar tracks. The streetscape is characterized by blank building frontages with security shutters and a fenced-off parking lot, which limits natural surveillance and pedestrian comfort.

hazards.name: Streetcar Tracks
hazards.description: Embedded tracks in the roadway pose a tripping hazard for pedestrians and a risk for cyclists.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Buffer
hazards.description: No physical separation between the sidewalk and the travel lane increases risk from passing vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Curb line

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: Solid metal shutters and high fencing reduce natural surveillance and eyes on the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Building ground floor and adjacent lot

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer
interventions.description: Install street trees or furniture to create a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crossing
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crossing with signage to provide a designated safe point for pedestrians to cross.

interventions.title: Frontage Activation
interventions.description: Encourage active ground-floor uses and transparent storefronts to improve the pedestrian experience and safety.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, but lacks marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures. The presence of trolley tracks in the roadway and on-street parking creates potential tripping hazards and sightline obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Embedded metal tracks in the roadway can be slippery when wet and pose a tripping hazard for pedestrians crossing mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway extending into the distance

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb block the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the curb

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: A large blank wall on the left side of the street reduces natural surveillance and can make the environment feel less safe.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side building facade

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Add a marked mid-block crossing with continental markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture
interventions.description: Add street trees and benches on the left side to activate the blank frontage and provide a buffer from traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a continuous, well-maintained sidewalk adjacent to a building and a construction site. While the walkway is clear, the presence of parallel parked vehicles and solid fencing creates visual obstructions that may impact safety at crossing points.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: The parked SUV blocks the view of the roadway for pedestrians, especially children or those using mobility devices, who might need to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, left side

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Fencing
hazards.description: The solid construction fencing and posters limit visibility into the adjacent lot, potentially hiding hazards or reducing natural surveillance.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right side, along the sidewalk edge

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points or site access to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees/Buffer
